experiment.name: early_power_reveal
experiment.change: Explicitly state the hero's core power or identity within the first three shots immediately following the hook.
experiment.rationale: Establishing the protagonist's specific stakes and abilities early will ground viewer context before the main conflict escalates.

experiment.name: sensory_onomatopoeia_emphasis
experiment.change: Incorporate at least one onomatopoeia sound effect from the comic panel directly into the narration text of that shot.
experiment.rationale: Adding sensory sound words to the narration increases engagement by mimicking the comic book reading experience.

experiment.name: ultra_short_middle_shot
experiment.change: Include exactly one 2-word shot in the middle of the video to create a sharp pacing drop.
experiment.rationale: Sudden rhythm shifts keep viewer retention high on YouTube Shorts by disrupting predictability.

experiment.name: dialogue_hook
experiment.change: Start the hook with a direct quote from a speech balloon in the first panel.
experiment.rationale: Using an in-world quote immediately immerses the viewer into the action faster than third-person exposition.

experiment.name: color_coded_keywords
experiment.change: Highlight key nouns in yellow to draw visual focus to plot-critical objects in the captions.
experiment.rationale: Color-coding key nouns helps viewers quickly grasp the central conflict and objects of interest in fast-paced Shorts.

experiment.name: tighter_duration_target
experiment.change: Cap total video duration under 45 seconds by keeping narration strictly between 80 and 110 words total.
experiment.rationale: Shorter Golden Age recaps prevent mid-video drop-off and boost completion rate on YouTube Shorts.

experiment.name: action_verb_titles
experiment.change: Use an imperative action verb at the start of the title to heighten immediate curiosity.
experiment.rationale: Starting titles with high-energy action verbs can boost initial click-through rates on short-form feeds.

experiment.name: question_hook
experiment.change: Start the hook with a direct question addressing the viewer to boost initial engagement.
experiment.rationale: Direct questions create a cognitive open loop that forces viewers to watch further to find the answer.

experiment.name: color_coded_captions
experiment.change: Use blue text for hero dialogue and white text for narrator narration.
experiment.rationale: Differentiating speaker types visually helps viewers follow the narrative flow faster.

experiment.name: cliffhanger_transitions
experiment.change: End the penultimate shot with a question that is answered by the final image.
experiment.rationale: Cliffhangers encourage viewers to watch the final frame, increasing retention.

experiment.name: strict_emphasis_ratio
experiment.change: Limit visual emphasis (red, green, cyan) to exactly one in every four shots.
experiment.rationale: Standardizing visual cues prevents viewer fatigue and ensures high-impact moments remain distinct.

experiment.name: ultra_short_beats
experiment.change: Cap every single shot's narration at a maximum of 4 words to maximize hyper-fast YouTube Shorts pacing.
experiment.rationale: Shorter beats increase retention and align better with rapid-fire word-by-word caption styles.

experiment.name: concise_hook
experiment.change: Limit the hook question to a maximum of 6 words.
experiment.rationale: Shorter, punchier hook questions capture viewer attention faster in the first 2 seconds.

experiment.name: cliffhanger_penultimate_shot
experiment.change: The second-to-last shot must be a narrator question in white text, followed by a silent 2-second final panel showing the visual answer.
experiment.rationale: Creating a brief moment of silence for the visual payoff can increase the impact of the consequence and improve loop-back retention.

experiment.name: hero_first_word_hook
experiment.change: Start the hook question with the superhero's full name as the first two words.
experiment.rationale: Leading immediately with a recognizable hero name increases instant viewer familiarity and retention.

experiment.name: two_character_dialogue_shots
experiment.change: Include at least two shots containing hero dialogue transcribed verbatim from speech balloons and rendered with blue captions.
experiment.rationale: Direct character speech breaks up third-person narration and leverages the highest-performing video's color-coded caption mechanic to boost retention.

experiment.name: midpoint_twist_reveal_beat
experiment.change: Place a single green-emphasized plot reveal shot exactly at the midpoint (shots 14-16) of the narration arc.
experiment.rationale: Anchoring a major narrative turning point at the exact midpoint prevents mid-video retention drop-offs in 120-second formats.

experiment.name: red_danger_hook_emphasis
experiment.change: Ensure the first shot (hook) always uses red danger emphasis on the primary threat words.
experiment.rationale: High-performing videos leverage early danger signals to immediately draw viewers in during the first 2 seconds.

experiment.name: strict_seven_word_hook
experiment.change: Enforce a strict maximum limit of 7 words for the opening hook narration sentence.
experiment.rationale: Data reveals top-performing videos average 7.0 hook words compared to 8.5 in bottom performers, ensuring immediate retention.

experiment.name: action_verb_hook_card
experiment.change: Ensure the ALL-CAPS hook card contains at least one active physical combat verb.
experiment.rationale: High-impact action words on the thumbnail card increase initial click-through and viewer curiosity.

experiment.name: action_verb_hook_card
experiment.change: Ensure the 3-6 word ALL-CAPS hook card contains at least one active physical combat verb (e.g., PUNCHES, STRIKES, TRAPS, DESTROYS).
experiment.rationale: Empirical top performers lead with high physical conflict in early seconds, and action verbs heighten initial visual click-through.

experiment.rationale: High-performing videos lead with immediate kinetic combat, and a physical combat verb in the hook card sharpens viewer urgency.

experiment.name: target_shot_count
experiment.change: Strictly target 23 to 24 shots per video to align directly with top-performing metrics.
experiment.rationale: Top-performing videos average 23.5 shots, indicating this specific length optimizes viewer retention and pacing.

experiment.name: famous_hero_focus
experiment.change: Focus narration exclusively on a globally famous hero name in the title and hook instead of obscure Golden Age titles.
experiment.rationale: High-performing videos leverage widely recognized names to dramatically improve click-through rates and early retention.

experiment.name: all_caps_danger_beats
experiment.change: Render all red 'danger' emphasis captions in ALL-CAPS to distinguish them from normal narration.
experiment.rationale: Visual differentiation of high-stakes moments can increase viewer arousal and retention during peak action sequences.

experiment.name: red_emphasis_first_shot
experiment.change: Apply a red 'danger' emphasis color to the very first shot narration beat instead of normal text.
experiment.rationale: Immediate visual visual cues on frame one increase high-stakes viewer arousal and early retention.

experiment.name: cyan_reversal_penultimate_shot
experiment.change: Set the penultimate shot (shot N-1) to cyan reversal emphasis directly before the final consequence beat.
experiment.rationale: Marking a distinct narrative turning point right before the final impact maximizes tension and sharpens the abrupt cold consequence ending.

experiment.name: strict_six_word_hook
experiment.change: Enforce a strict maximum limit of exactly 6 words for the opening sentence hook.
experiment.rationale: Data shows top-performing videos favor shorter hooks (mean 8.0 vs 8.7), and tightening to 6 words accelerates viewer hook retention in the critical first 2 seconds.

experiment.name: concrete_number_in_first_three_shots
experiment.change: Include at least one concrete numerical stat (seconds, km/s, or degrees) within the first three shots.
experiment.rationale: Early concrete numbers establish grounded scale immediately and boost early viewer engagement.

experiment.name: strict_numerical_pacing_50_percent
experiment.change: Include at least one concrete numerical stat (seconds, degrees, km/s, or times Earth) in exactly 50% or more of all shot beats.
experiment.rationale: High density of visceral numbers grounds speculative scenarios and sustains audience curiosity throughout the entire duration.

experiment.name: extreme_punchy_beats_max_six_words
experiment.change: Cap every single shot beat at a maximum of 6 words across the entire video script.
experiment.rationale: Tighter word bounds increase pacing kineticism and improve subtitle-speech alignment for fast short-form audience retention.

experiment.name: strict_five_word_beats
experiment.change: Enforce a strict maximum of 5 words on every single shot beat throughout the script.
experiment.rationale: Narrowing beat length further accelerates narration delivery speed toward top-performing short-form pacing standards.

experiment.name: opening_countdown_metric
experiment.change: Include an exact time countdown metric in seconds within the very first shot narration beat.
experiment.rationale: Immediate countdown metrics create urgent stakes on frame one to boost initial short retention.

experiment.name: opening_countdown_metric
experiment.change: Include an exact time countdown metric in seconds within the very first shot narration beat.
experiment.rationale: Immediate countdown metrics create urgent stakes on frame one to boost initial short retention.

experiment.name: tight_emphasis_cap
experiment.change: Strictly cap total colored emphasis beats to at most 18% of total shots.
experiment.rationale: Data shows top videos averaged 22% emphasis while bottom videos averaged 35%, suggesting fewer colored beats increases visual impact.

experiment.name: calibrated_title_length_window
experiment.change: Constrain the title strictly between 48 and 54 characters while maintaining the object and threat format.
experiment.rationale: Measured differences indicate top-performing videos average 53.8 characters compared to 56.0 characters for underperforming videos.

experiment.name: target_word_rate_120_wpm
experiment.change: Set narration word rate strictly to 120-125 words per minute across all shot beats.
experiment.rationale: Top-performing videos average 124.5 WPM while lower-performing videos average 130 WPM, showing clearer pacing drives retention.

experiment.name: target_title_length_52_chars
experiment.change: Target an exact title length between 50 and 54 characters centered on the top-performing 53.8 average.
experiment.rationale: Top-performing videos cluster tightly around 53.8 characters compared to 56.0 characters for underperforming videos.

experiment.name: cyan_penultimate_turn
experiment.change: Place a single cyan turn shot at beat N-1 to signal the final consequence.
experiment.rationale: Visual color shifts right before the climax prepare the viewer for the final consequence and boost loop retention.

experiment.name: consequence_final_transformation
experiment.change: End the final shot explicitly with an irreversible physical state transformation rather than a summary or question.
experiment.rationale: Grounded consequence closings reinforce visceral stakes and increase seamless looping retention.

experiment.name: target_exact_22_shots_duration
experiment.change: Lock target shot count to exactly 22 shots across 88 to 95 seconds.
experiment.rationale: Top-performing videos cluster tightly around an average of 22 shots and 92.6 seconds.
